title: Moment-only intervals included zero for six paired bird drought contrasts in a 2024 data release
abstract: We rebuilt six fledging-minus-egg drought response contrasts from a public bird data release. Two prior normal-reference upper limits were below zero. No upper limit based only on unbiased estimates and known variance bounds was below zero after six-test correction. Independent source-row errors also gave no corrected moment-only sign claim. We give explicit null error laws that attain the tail bounds under arbitrary within-study covariance. Row-wise additive errors of 0.00771 and 0.03470 source standardized units would remove the two normal exclusions. These are sensitivity thresholds, not measured biases. All observations overlap the prior study. Estimated source variances, small samples, different nests and denominators, and publication selection limit inference. The result tests uncertainty assumptions and does not show no drought effect. Code, proof, aggregate results, source hashes and a figure are included.

display.caption: All six one-sided moment-only intervals include zero. Limits condition on unbiased estimates and known variance bounds. Normal upper limits reproduce the prior two-sided calculation; moment-only limits are one-sided. Both use six-test correction.

citations.reason: We rebuild its six paired endpoint contrasts and test its stated normal-approximation limitation. All biological observations overlap.
Review of demographic metric and replication limits in the same public archive.
Prior probability-inequality work; the one-sided moment inequality is standard, not a new theorem here.
